Ordinarily this chamber, the native holy of helies, is in murky darkness, but Captain Hurley seized an opportunity when the whole vill-ago was attending a funeral, to enter it secretly. THE MEETING IN THE GREAT RAVI AT KAIMARY.

This solemn council meeting was convened in the 250 feet long, cavern-like vestibule of the great Ravi of Kaimari, to consider the request of Captain Hurley to purchase one of the mysterious bundles that lay under the holy Imumu. A few of the natives were willing that a bundle should disappear, providing a large knife was found in its place, but the majority of the meeting decided against this. In the end, however, monstrous bluff and generous gifts of Kuku (trade tobacco) softened the natives, and permission was given to the explorers to extract one bullroarer from each package ---- at the price of twenty more sticks of Kuku, and a present of rice. With the keeper of the Imumu, the two white men entered the sanctum, which lay at the end of the vestibule, and was concealed by a screen, which kept it in bat-filled semi-darkness. The high priest refused to touch the sacred packages, and Mr McCulloch, scientist of the Hurley expedition, had the task of opening them and selecting a bullroarer from each. The spiders, scorpions, centipedes, and other verin which crawled forth from each package did not make his task an enviable one.

After the selection was made, and wrapped up in palm leaf, none would venture near, nor would they allow the parcel to leave the Ravi until it was securely wrapped up in numerous sleeping-mats, with McCulloch's singlet over al. For should any gaze on the sacred bullroarers they would immediately die, or become violently ill.

Kaimari is the largest of the Purari Delta villages (Papua) and is situated in the middle of a fifty-mile mangrove swamp --- a dreary expense of mud and crazy desolation. The huts are built on piles, and are thatched with sago-palm leaves. The Styx Promenade (as Captain Hurley has named the main thoroughfare) is a rained roadway of ricetty, half-rotten mangrove sticks, which runs through the middle of Kaimari, spanning creeks and slime. From it pathways lead to the demiciles, enabling the inhabitants to move about without sinking thigh-deep in filth. The Styx Promenade leads to a colossal building, the Ravi or club house of Kaimari. A majestic, 50-foot arch stands imposingly facing the thoroughfare, and a barrier of woven palm-leaf screens the entrance from the curious, and maybe impious eye.
